So check out Displate at San Diego Comic-Con or in the link below the code Patherics to save 25% off one Dis Plate, 32% off two to three disc plates, and a whopping 37% off four plus disc plates. Grab your favorite design, and thanks to Displate for sponsoring today's journey. And so our journey in Redidge begins. For the first time in over 150 hours, we're somewhere new. And most importantly, new mobs and different loot tables. Now, as we mentioned in the last zone, in the spirit of the new unlock, we have flipped Chromy time to Cataclysm, which means the mobs here will continue to scale with us. So unlike Elwin, where Goldilock could one-shot pretty much any mob in his sleep, here in Redidge, we're actually fighting, and that changes everything.

source.quote: For one, I've had to read my tool tips for the first time in actually quite a while. So, the plan is simple. To start off in Red Ridge, we're going to run every quest in the zone, front to back, just to get our bearings and scout out the zone. We'll build a little bit of raw capital and pick along a few rares along the way. And of course, we're going to mine every vein and herb every brush that we see along the way. This is Recon, a little change of pace exploration, but with a purpose. It didn't take long for a problem to emerge. You see, back in Elwin, the mobs stopped scaling at level 30, and so did their drops, which means now we're over level 50, wearing a mismatched quilt of oldworld greens, most of which never scaled beyond level 25. We're missing pieces, we're missing stats, we're missing a little bit of everything. And the Red Ridge mobs, well, they don't care. This gets worse because not only are we undergeeared and pretty much getting down to 10% health after every mob, the vendors in both Elvin and Redidge still only sell low-level food, which does literally nothing to our over 50,000 health bar at this point. That kind of stuff barely healed us back when we level 12. So, for now, we're bruised.

source.quote: And while editing this, I realized TSM fully docked my new in-game name. So, yeah, I'll be doing another name change before this episode goes live and changing my tool tip settings on TSM. Anyway, with our first hour of Red Ridge Farming complete, brushing right up against the Chromy time scaling levels. And that just means it's time to fight some monsters while we're still on their level. And with that in mind, I made my way north into a cave that I had earmarked earlier while questing, Render's Rock. It has some tight corridors, a good ore density, and is crawling with black rock orcs. I wanted to give this place an hourong test run just to see what would drop and see how much ore we could pull in. So, inside the cave, there's two variants of Black Rockck Orcs. The Black Rock Trackers and the Black Rock summoners. Now, these are just two of maybe a dozen different Black Rockck mob types in the zone, each with their own little transmog table quirks. More on the others later. There are some big items for sure, but for this cave, we're hunting two things in particular. From the trackers, I was after the black rock puldrons. Albeit a white item, it's still fully transmogable and it's part of the Black Rock set that's a bit of a staple to the Red Ridge transmog scene. Now, Trade Skill Master is only listing a 0.05% drop rate, but they are valued at around a 5,000 gold market. And from the summoners, the prize that we're targeting is the Black Rock boots.

source.quote: Another 0.05% drop rate, but way rarer on the market with a floating value around 35,000 gold. So, how'd we do? Well, let's just say the first tracker we killed dropped the puldrons. No warm-up, no buildup, just boom, target acquired on pull one. And then 16 minutes into our farm, we nailed the boots. No kidding. Two rare drops in the first 16 minutes. Now, I'll note briefly here that TSM is showing the region sale averages on both, which will often be quite a bit lower than the market value just from people listing these when they don't know the true value that they can hold. But even if we don't get peak market price, we're still in the green here. And then around the 30 minute mark of the farm, something kind of weird happened. The gold perk kill dropped from about two gold perk kill down to 30 silver. And the loot seemed to start drying up. Fewer greens and fewer drops overall. I think this might be the openw world loot tables acting a bit weirdly, but in this instance, it almost seemed like they fed us the loot that we wanted right up front and then pulled it back. After the full hour of farming, we did manage to actually snag a second pair of puldrons.

source.quote: First up, the murloc scouts. They may look like a classic murloc, but that blade, well, it's on the drop table, and it's called the scimitar of a tune. A sleek curved semi with a reported drop rate of 0.03%. And as some travelers mentioned in the comments, we can download the Wowhead elooter add-on, which means every kill we log here and every piece of loot we get will get uploaded onto the Wowhead database and update the real-time drop rates. And the second target is the Merurloc Tide Collar. This one doesn't carry a semi, but has a staff, and that staff is also on the drop table, the Riverside staff. This one is also reporting a 0.03% drop rate. still a commanding 42,000 gold on the auction house for market value. And we're not AoE farming these guys yet. These mobs will fight back and we'll continue to gain XP until we get level 70 or 71. And to track it all personally, I'm running Kill Tracker. So, we'll have a live tally on how many of each murloc we've got. No guesses, no estimates.

records.summary: Exits scaling and adapts vineyard macro for much faster one-shot target farming; not separate measured GPH.

source.quote: Goldilocked is now officially a datadriven farmer. And after an hour or so of farming, we did hit level 69 and totaled 51 kills on the scouts. and 41 kills on the tide collars. And while we did snag a few lower tier transmog pieces, some grays with a little bit of potential, our white whales of the scimitar of a tune and the riverside staff were nowhere to be seen. So I guess that's it, right? We pack it up, give up, and log off. Nope. We double down. And while killing these guys mixed in with a few rares, we hit level 70. And with chromy time scaling in the rear view, we started absolutely one-shotting these murlocs. I even dusted off and upgraded the old Elwin bore farming macro, the live to win. Every pull was faster and cleaner, so the murlocs never stood a chance. And I won't lie to you.

source.quote: Shoulders check, boots, check. All right, but enough waiting. Let's get to the loot. There we go. Over 130 males. and even just the first 100 is stacked with some serious value. Now, a lot of the recent ones coming through are a handful of the raw mats, the herbs and ores that we got here from our side hustles. Although, to be fair, in this episode, we didn't do much gathering. Most of our time was poured into leveling and transmog hunting. And speaking of transmog, we actually sold both scimitars of a tune, a little sneaky null punisher that we picked up while leveling. But we were a little bit cheeky in the sales here. I listed these at fire sale prices around 7K. This is just for some early gold injection to the challenge to get things moving. You know how it is. I can always go back and farm some more. But that wasn't the end of it. We also moved a pair of burnished boots, a leveling drop from the zone, and a few options trickled in from the tail end of Elwin.
